behavioral_effects: The typed graph vocabulary is now a committed reviewed contract: 11 node types and 9 edge types with required edge provenance fields, catalogued and schema-validated; extractors in sessions 6.2-6.4 emit only declared kinds.
compatibility_impact: graph-model.schema.json widened, not broken: the reserved form still validates (pinned by a dedicated test) and no committed document used the old strict shape. Kernel bindings for the node-types and edge-types split were already committed and are now satisfied.
follow_up: Stop-hook caught the vocabulary documents carrying a $schema key the schema did not declare; fixed by mirroring the local-governance schema convention. Consider a lint that every schema with additionalProperties false declares $schema.
limitations: Vocabulary only - no extractor emits the new kinds yet; the import graph continues to emit its original three edge kinds.
reason: Phase 6 needs the typed node and edge vocabulary as reviewed instances, but graph-model.schema.json was reserved and required both arrays in one document while the kernel bindings expect a node-types and edge-types split; the schema now admits the split and the vocabulary the import graph already conforms to is committed
risks: The vocabulary is declared ahead of most extractors; kinds that prove wrong in 6.2-6.4 must be revised there rather than worked around.
rollback: git revert of the single commit; removes the two vocabulary files, restores the reserved schema, and drops the catalog, read-surface, and ownership entries with it.
security_impact: None. The vocabulary declares graph kinds; no permission, exposure, or code path changed. The tool node type states that per-user MCP edges stay runtime-evidence only, matching existing policy.
summary: Commit the graph vocabulary and activate the graph-model schema
